description_full: Inter & Co, Inc., through its subsidiaries, engages in the banking and spending, investments, insurance brokerage, and inter shop businesses in Brazil and the United States. The company offers banking products and services, including checking accounts; cards; deposits; loans and advances; and other services, as well as debt collections; foreign exchange and financial services; and global account digital solution. It also provides acquisition, sale, and custody of securities; structures and distributes securities; and operates management of fund portfolios and other assets. In addition, the company offers insurance products including warranties, life, property, and automobile insurance; pension products; and consortium products. Further, it engages in the sale of goods and/or services through digital platform. Inter & Co, Inc. was founded in 1994 and is headquartered in Belo Horizonte, Brazil.

financial_summary: Inter & Co. Inc. is a small-cap financial services business with a $1.8B market cap on $1.2B of annual revenue.

The top line has compounded at +43% over the past three years, the kind of sustained demand persistence that marks a compounder. Operating margins are expanding by +9.7pp year-over-year, which is one of the strongest signals that the moat is deepening.
Returns on capital run at 3% against a 9% cost of capital, which means the business is destroying value with every dollar it reinvests.

The business throws off $686M in free cash flow — roughly 57 cents on every revenue dollar, which is the owner-earnings figure that actually belongs to shareholders, and cash conversion sits at 3.86× so those profits are backed by real cash.

On the balance sheet, the balance sheet carries net cash, which is the gold standard: the business never has to make desperate decisions in a bad year, and thin 0.4× interest coverage leaves no room for a bad year.
Shareholder yield is only 1.0%, a thin return of capital, and insiders hold 25% of the shares, so management thinks like owners because it is one — the strongest alignment there is.
